clue.text: Show off, getting first of reds in pocket

indicators.note: in places the picked letter within the pocket word

parts.note: a pocket is a small bag or pouch

indicators.note: first of picks out the opening letter of the word reds

explanation.surface: A snooker player boasts after potting a red into a pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: The snooker picture of reds and pockets is misdirection; the pocket is just a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: To boast about yourself is to show off, a plain synonym pair.

clue.text: Reading squad reserve with green gear

parts.note: to reserve a table or seat is to book it
a golf club is equipment used on the golf course's green

explanation.surface: A sports team from the town of Reading keeps reserves and green kit.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading looks like the English town with a football team; it is the pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: A group meeting to discuss books it has all read is a reading group, playfully called a squad.

clue.text: It snakes around Canada with no bends!

indicators.note: bends signals that the letters are twisted out of their order

explanation.surface: A tongue-in-cheek boast about a river or road through Canada running dead straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It snakes' sounds like a winding path, but it means the creature itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The anaconda is a huge South American constrictor, so it is literally a snake.

clue.text: Kind of cleaner I propped against piece of furniture

indicators.note: propped against says the next piece sits right beside the previous ones

parts.note: a char or charwoman is a British term for a cleaning lady
a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady describes leaning a type of object against a table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of' reads as 'type of', but 'Kind' alone is the adjective; CHAR is a dated British word for a cleaning woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Being generous and benevolent towards others is a synonym for being kind.

clue.text: Times delivered by hotel for us

parts.note: Hotel is the NATO alphabet word for H
something meant for us is ours

explanation.surface: Newspapers are being delivered to a hotel for the guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' suggests the newspaper delivered to a hotel; it is plural time periods.
explanation.definitionFit: Periods of the clock, as in opening hours, are times.

clue.text: Official position number, e.g. Ist, rarely includes it

indicators.note: includes it says the clue words before it hold the solution within them

parts.note: the letters run across the words; the digit 1 is read as the Roman numeral I, so 1st is written IST

explanation.surface: A rule about how a numbered position such as first is officially written.
explanation.walkthrough: The digit 1 is read as the letter I, so numbeR E.G. 1ST RARely gives the letters; 'it' just points at the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A registrar records births, marriages and deaths, an official post in local government.

clue.text: Something enhancing taste in mouth after salt used twice

indicators.note: after says the cheek word comes behind the sailors
used twice says the word for salt is written two times in a row

parts.note: a salt or a tar is an old sailor
mouth and sauce both mean cheeky backchat

explanation.surface: A recipe note about flavour building in the mouth after salting twice.
explanation.walkthrough: Salt and taste suggest seasoning, but salt is a sailor; SAUCE is British slang for cheek, as is mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: This mayonnaise-based condiment served with fish is a dressing that improves flavour.

clue.text: VIP in major cover-up, that's hairy

parts.note: major means big or important
a wig is a hairy covering for the head

explanation.surface: A celebrity is caught in a big scandal with a hairy cover-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover-up' suggests a scandal; it is a hairpiece covering a bald head.
explanation.definitionFit: An important person, a bigshot or grandee, is informally called by this term.

clue.text: Rambling harangue in support of Her Majesty

indicators.note: in a down answer a piece in support of another sits beneath it

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
a harangue is a ranting speech

explanation.surface: A long, rambling speech made in support of the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'in support of' puts RANT below ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Wandering or roving, as in a knight errant, is to be rambling.

clue.text: Authorise oxygen gas from the East

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

indicators.note: from the East says the word is read from right to left, as east lies to the right on a map

parts.note: to gas is to chatter idly, to yak

explanation.surface: An instruction to approve a supply of oxygen gas coming from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxygen gas reads as one chemical; 'gas' is idle chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: To give approval or sign off on something is to authorise it, informally.

clue.text: Shift gear with artist backing little singer

parts.note: to budge is to shift or move
rig is equipment or gear

indicators.note: backing says the artist abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A singer's backing band moves its gear around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing singer' tempts as a phrase; 'backing' reverses RA to AR.
explanation.definitionFit: This small Australian parakeet, a popular caged pet, chirps and sings.

clue.text: Idiot — that man has 1 Across the wrong way round!

definitions.note: the answer to 1 Across reversed gives garb, meaning dress

parts.note: a clot is a British word for a fool
he's is short for he has

explanation.surface: Someone calls a man a fool for boasting backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1 Across answer, BRAG, reversed is GARB, meaning attire.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is a word for one's outfit or attire, which is what we wear.

clue.text: Using horsewhip or alternative, show strong feelings about somebody

indicators.note: an alternative form of the words means their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Strong feelings are being shown with a whip or something else.
explanation.definitionFit: To idolise and adore someone admiringly expresses intense feeling towards them.

clue.text: Stop using toast in cooking

indicators.note: cooking signals that the letters are prepared afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction to quit using toast in cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' reads as a verb; it is a noun, a place where a train halts.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway or bus stopping place is a halt, another word for a stop.

clue.text: Junior to sidestep second 11

definitions.note: the 11 Across answer means apparel, and these are examples of it

parts.note: someone junior to another is under them
to skirt an issue is to sidestep it

explanation.surface: A junior player is told to sidestep the second eleven team.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' looks like a sports team; it points to the answer at 11 Across, CLOTHES.
explanation.definitionFit: Petticoats worn beneath a dress are examples of garments.

clue.text: Famous war lord in hot place, tracked by eastern resistance

indicators.note: tracked by says the following pieces come after

parts.note: a kitchen is a hot room with ovens
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A notorious warlord hides in a hot place, pursued by eastern rebels.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Kitchener was the British war secretary of the First World War, famous from the 'Your country needs you' poster.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbert Kitchener was an earl and British field marshal, so literally a lord of war.

clue.text: Caption I designed, one that helps people see …

indicators.note: designed says the letters are arranged into a new design

explanation.surface: A picture caption written to help people see what is shown.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye-care professional tests vision and supplies glasses, aiding sight.

clue.text: … what's prescribed by 16 as gel — yes, that's unusual

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: An optician prescribes something as a gel, and the patient agrees it is odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 is OPTICIAN, and the two clues run on with the ellipsis.
explanation.definitionFit: A monocle or lens for one eye is something an eye specialist might recommend.

clue.text: Facility that AA members may be driven to use?

definitions.text: Facility that AA members may be driven to use?

parts.words: Facility that AA members may be driven to use?
parts.note: AA suggests the British motoring organisation, but here it is Alcoholics Anonymous, whose members turn to non-alcoholic drinks

explanation.surface: A roadside service that motoring club members might drive to.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is also Britain's Automobile Association, which makes 'driven' look like motoring.
explanation.definitionFit: A source of drinking water is a utility provision that a teetotaller relies on.

clue.text: Composes ceremonies by ear

indicators.note: by ear says the word is judged as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: rites are ceremonies

explanation.surface: A musician composes ceremonial music by ear.
explanation.definitionFit: To pen music or words is to compose them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Combat guns get mislaid regularly — that's stupid

indicators.note: mislaid regularly says every other letter is lost, keeping the rest

explanation.surface: A soldier complains about losing combat guns time after time.
explanation.definitionFit: Slow to understand, dull-witted, is a synonym of stupid.

clue.text: New start in river race — overturned, hospital to follow

indicators.note: to follow says the hospital letter comes last
overturned says the word for race is turned upside down

parts.note: a race of people is a tribe

explanation.surface: A boat overturns in a river race and the crew go to hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' suggests a contest on the river, but it is a people; overturned TRIBE gives EBIRT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being born again, a renaissance, is a fresh beginning.

clue.text: Time to be part of campaign I never rejected

indicators.note: rejected says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says the letters lie within the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A campaigner says it is time to join a campaign they once turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Time to be part' as the definition, but 'part of' is the hidden-word indicator and 'Time' alone the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The later part of the day after afternoon is a time of day.

clue.text: Prompt breakfast could be this followed by toast

definitions.meaning: to prompt or urge someone on

definitions.text: breakfast could be this followed by toast
definitions.meaning: a breakfast dish of eggs is served on toast

explanation.surface: A prompt breakfast of eggs and toast.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge or encourage someone is the phrasal verb meaning prompt; add toast and it is breakfast.

clue.text: Meet with work in the balance

parts.note: things that touch meet
and means together with
a machine that works is said to go

explanation.surface: A meeting about work whose outcome is undecided.
explanation.definitionFit: When the outcome is uncertain and risky it hangs precariously, undecided.

clue.text: Somewhere in Italy having a drink, falling over

indicators.note: falling over says the pieces are turned the other way

parts.note: to sip is to drink

explanation.surface: A tourist in Italy has a drink and falls over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling over' hints at the city's famous leaning tower as well.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tuscan city famous for its leaning tower is a place in Italy.

clue.text: Proceeding with different partner contracted as relative

parts.note: a step is a proceeding or measure taken

indicators.note: different signals that the remaining letters are rearranged
contracted says the word is shortened by losing its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone moves on with a new partner, as a contract for a family relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracted' cuts PARTNER to PARTNE, which 'different' rearranges into PARENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent by marriage rather than by blood is a family member.

clue.text: More than one goal post moving front to back

indicators.note: moving front to back says the first letter goes to the end

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it

explanation.surface: A footballer's goalpost is shifted from front to back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goal post' reads as one football fixture; they are separate words with separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Aims or purposes are ends, as in ends and means, here plural goals.
